correctness.rationale: Spatial Fourier Parseval reduces the quartic moment to lag-correlation squares. Distinct cubic lag frequencies differ exactly by 3hr(2m+h+r)>0 in the stated domain, so continuous time annihilates all off-diagonal terms. Uniform N-grid averaging retains precisely those divisible by N, and conjugate pairing produces factor four. The t/gcd modular congruence detects every admissible alias including boundaries. All-ones coefficients prove necessity and the strict sharp-constant transition; coefficient Cauchy-Schwarz gives the no-alias sharp constant and its extremizers. For primes >=2K-3 none of h,r,2m+h+r is divisible by p; primes below cutoff have the explicit collision (1,2,(p-3)/2) for p>=5, while p=2,3 use (1,1,0). The executable checks 1344 exact modular cases, 756 direct real quartics, 88 complex quartics and 32 prime cutoffs. Finite tests corroborate, not prove, the universal identity.

value.rationale: Exact finite observation of quartic dispersive Fourier evolution is structurally natural, not a renamed numerical exercise. The theorem resolves every arbitrary-complex-coefficient instance on a standard positive cubic Fourier band for all grid moduli by an efficient congruence test, gives the exact sharp-norm preservation transition, and identifies the sharp minimal prime grid size linear in the number of modes despite cubic temporal frequencies. Signed alias terms and exceptional small bands are material boundary conditions.
